cohort: 250 obese and 250 non-obese women giving birth for the first time
finding: Obese and non-obese women who went into labour spontaneously at term had similar rates of labour augmentation, length of active labour, emergency caesarean delivery, postpartum haemorrhage and OASIS, despite higher rates of comorbidities among the obese women.
mod_finding: There was no significant difference in the proportion of vaginal deliveries between obese (72%) and non-obese (78%) women.
